_comment: Help screen text, English. Sections appear in this order. 'art' is a row of emoji drawn as the section's picture. Text may use {riceEaten} and {gatherPerClick}, filled in from content/rules.json so the numbers never go stale. Translations live next to this file with the same section ids.
label: English

sections.title: Your goal
body: You are a new datu. Grow a small barangay by the river into a thriving settlement.
Gather, build, and look after your people. Later, bring the neighboring barangays to your side, by friendship or by force.

sections.title: Food, Palay and wood
body: Tap Forage or Gather Wood for +{gatherPerClick} each time.

Every villager eats {riceEaten} Pagkain (everyday food) a second: gabi, yams, millet, bananas, sago, coconuts, fish and meat. If the food runs out, they eat Palay, which wastes it; with nothing left, nobody works and after a while families leave.

Food is kept the old way: root crops stay in the Gabihan and Kaingin (they don't spoil and survive typhoons), fish live in a Baklad, each house smokes and salts fresh food into its jars, and the Kamalig holds Palay, dried goods and Asin. Fresh food left out spoils.
A varied diet (starches, fish, meat, fruit and greens) makes people happier. Eating one kind for too long makes them unhappy and sickly.
Palay (rice) is a prestige grain: for offerings, gifts, marriage alliances, rice wine and the Pista at the Bahay ng Datu.
Tap a resource at the top to see where it comes from and where it goes.

sections.title: Buildings and workers
body: Pick a building from the bar at the bottom, then tap a highlighted tile. Each copy costs a bit more than the last.
A Bahay Kubo houses more villagers. New families arrive while there is room and food.
Healthy villagers go to work on their own, filling the fields and camps. Tap a building to see who works there, or to move or demolish it.

Tap forest next to your land to select it (or drag across it with a mouse), then press Clear. Each tile costs a little Pagkain upfront, and free villagers clear them one by one. Tap a tile being cleared to stop it.

sections.title: Seasons and events
body: The year turns between Tag-ulan, the rainy season, and Tag-araw, the dry season, when the fields yield less. The dry season hurts rice and gabi most; yams, millet and sago hold up. Rough seas cut fishing, and typhoons flatten bananas and rice, but root crops in the ground survive.
Typhoons are announced before they strike: keep wood for repairs. Tap a burning house to put the fire out before it spreads. Sickness keeps villagers from work; a Babaylan's hut helps them heal.

sections.title: The Rehiyon
body: Open the Rehiyon map to meet the other barangays of the archipelago. Each has its own datu, tradition and temperament, and many belong to alliances.
Barangays on your own island are a walk away. To reach another island, build a Balangay Dock and train a Balangay: trades, gifts and raids then sail there and back, which takes time.

Trade: swap rice and wood. It builds trust and influence. Marriage alliance: once trust is high, a marriage ties your families together. Sandugo: a blood compact makes an ally who helps defend you. Neighbors also send trade offers that fit where they live: the coast offers Asin and fish for hardwood, Palay and gold; upriver barangays offer gold, root crops and hardwood for Asin and fish; one after a poor harvest or a flood asks for food. Each offer says why, and its worth in gold, the measure of value. Palay is valued highly.

Mangayaw (raid): train Mandirigma warriors and raid a rival for tribute. Raids win influence but cost trust with everyone, and the barangay you raid holds a grudge: it may counter or refuse your trades, refuse alliances, or stop trading altogether. A Handog (peace gift) eases a grudge. Raiders land on the river bank or beach, often at night or dawn, and prefer places no one watches.

Defense: a Bantayan (watchtower) at the shore, with its lookouts at work, sees raiders landing within its sight: you get a longer warning, the landing shows on the map at once and the alarm sounds. Unwatched, the warning is short and the landing shows only as the boats come close. A Kuta (palisaded refuge) near the Bahay ng Datu is where your Mandirigma rally before marching to the landing: those who get there in time fight, and those with time to spare are ready. Families within a Kuta's shelter take refuge, and raiders take much less from storehouses and fields there. Allies and tributaries send warriors too. The Defense map (Depensa tab) shows it all. Each Kuta allows 6 Mandirigma, never more than 30% of your villagers. When raiders come, only the Mandirigma the food workplaces can spare answer the call; "Call everyone" on the raid warning sends them all, and the fields stand empty until it's over.

When a neighbor's influence is full, they become your tributary and send part of their harvest. Keep them loyal, or they rebel. From a larger Bahay ng Datu you can form or join an alliance. Bring every barangay to your side to become Paramount Datu.

sections.title: Renown, levels and the Ranggo
body: Your barangay earns Kabantugan (renown) as it grows: every 10 villagers, each finished task, raids won and beaten off, trades, feasts, warriors' honor, answering an ally's call, a new tributary or ally (once for each barangay), a bigger Bahay ng Datu, and each Aklat entry (the first tasks and entries give a little, later ones more). Renown is never lost.

Trades, feasts and fighting (raids, defenses, honor and ally calls) give only so much renown each day; the higher your level, the more they can give. Once a kind has given its share, it gives none until the next day (about 10 hours of game time; time away counts). Growing the barangay, tasks and the Aklat are never limited.
Renown raises the barangay's level (shown by the ⭐ at the top). Each new level brings a gift, sometimes a title for your datu, and a bigger Bahay ng Datu needs a high enough level.
Tap the ⭐ to open the Ranggo ng Kapuluan: every barangay in the archipelago ranked by renown, by raids beaten off and by Aklat entries. When two are level, the one that got there first ranks higher.

Tap Bisitahin on any barangay in the Rehiyon to visit and look around their village. Looking changes nothing: you can trade, send a gift, talk alliances, or plan a raid and see where it would land before you send it. Bumalik brings you home.
